note: DRAFT E16 predictions from the lowduty calibration (N=1 baselines + class probes, one N=256 cal rung per arm) and the long rung (SPEC §6 step 2). To be reviewed and sealed with the user before the first measured ladder rung (PLAN Task 7 Step 4). Generated by e16/analysis/make_predictions.py.

calibration.host: AWS m7i.metal-24xl, 96 vCPU, 377 GiB, /srv/e15 XFS reflink

predictions.claim: The hypothesis (SPEC §7.2) is FALSIFIED: SBX's N_max is at or below resident ∞'s. Predicted ranges: SBX N_max in [576, 768]; resident ∞ N_max in [768, 1024] (ladder top 1024).
predictions.metric: assembled ladder.json n_max per arm at point lowduty (primary verdict, seeds by majority; e16/rig/chainlib.py)
predictions.falsifiedBy: n_max(SBX) ≥ one ladder step above n_max(resident ∞) (the hypothesis holds); separately, either arm's n_max outside its range falsifies the numeric part
predictions.note: Both arms are latency-limited and memory is far from binding (prediction 3). At N=256 both cal rungs hold with wide margins (SBX p95 excess 137 ms vs limit 336; resident 108 vs 395) on 2.95 / 2.81 slice cores. SBX: slope reading 648, per-session-load reading [596, 715]. Resident ∞: slope reading 942, per-session-load reading [799, 998]. The E15 metal ordering (resident 128 > SBX 80, both on condition 4) is expected to persist: at equal cores resident's p95 excess is lower (no per-call cold VM), and low duty lowers both arms' load per session alike (cores/session SBX 0.0115 vs resident 0.0110), so it does not change who reaches the limit first. The ranges overlap; a tie within one ladder step also falsifies the hypothesis.

predictions.claim: Each arm's first failed rung fails on condition 4 (added latency, class-matched p95 excess over the limit) with 0 failed calls, no refusal, and no memory verdict; host CPU mean below 25% there.
predictions.metric: record.json at each arm's first failed rung (stopped_at): conditions, failed_calls, refusals, binding/reason, samples host_cpu_busy_pct mean
predictions.falsifiedBy: either arm's first failed rung failing any other condition, any memory verdict (memory_floor, memory_high, host-memory refusal, OOM in e15.slice), or host CPU mean ≥ 25%
predictions.note: E15 metal: every first failure was condition 4 at 9–13% host CPU. At lowduty N=256 host CPU is 3.7% (SBX) and 3.3% (resident) mean. If an arm's ladder tops out at 1024 without failing, this prediction is not tested for that arm.

predictions.claim: Resident ∞'s physical memory at its N_max stays below 50% of host RAM (189 GiB): summed VM memory.current at the N_max rung's window peak in [109, 163] GiB at the predicted N_max range.
predictions.metric: max over the N_max rung's window of sum(samples.jsonl vm_mem) (GiB), and of slice_mem_bytes
predictions.falsifiedBy: summed VM memory ≥ 189 GiB at resident ∞'s N_max rung, or any memory verdict on a resident rung
predictions.note: Long rung (N=256, 3 h): median VM memory 0 min 61.9, 20 min 118.4, 60 min 142.4, 120 min 147.9, 180 min 147.1 MiB (a plateau after ~60 min; the paired 20→180 min +91% is selection: long-lived sessions are lighter at 20 min). At 2.5 h: 256 VMs, median 148.9, p95 233.1, max 292.0 MiB, sum 36.5 GiB; slice (worker + VMs) peak 41511 MiB = 162 MiB per VM. The band's session spans: median 5 min, p90 5.2 h; a session replayed from a random call has 82 min left on average, so few VMs pass 3 h (memory beyond 3 h is extrapolated flat). Physical memory bound: 1530 (every VM at the p95) to 2352 (at the measured per-VM slice) sessions, above the 1024 ladder top: memory does not bind resident ∞ at this duty.

predictions.claim: The driver uses less than 1% of host CPU at every E16 rung (A2).
predictions.metric: record.json driver.a2_pct_of_host, max over every E16 rung
predictions.note: N=256 cal rungs: 0.0169% (SBX), 0.0141% (resident); E15 metal max 0.0229% over 43 rungs. Linear to N=1024 gives < 0.1%.

admission_note: SPEC §7.3, a calculation, not a verdict: moca's default no-overcommit admission charges each VM 1056 MiB against host RAM (377 GiB), i.e. at most 365 live VMs. Resident ∞ holds one VM per session, so default admission would refuse it above N ≈ 365. SBX's live VMs at N=256 were 149 median / 184 p99 in the window (0.72 per session at p99; window max 192; the run's start, all 256 sessions launched within the 60 s spread, peaked at 703 live VMs), so in steady state it would be refused above N ≈ 508, and the start-up burst would be refused earlier. With admission as configured by default, SBX would hold more sessions than resident ∞ — the effect E16's 4 TiB budget removes on purpose (SPEC §1.2).
